_source: docs/DYNAMIC-GATE-PLAN.md: every gate row's numbers, their ranges and their provenance. scripts/gate_profiles.py builds ROWS from this file; no number here is duplicated in Python.
_rules: `default` is what a piece is judged by until its own profile or score says otherwise; `low`/`high` bound a profile's or a score's override, so no number can switch a row off.

`source` is either the citation the number came from or the words "starting value" when no published measurement exists. Every parameter carries one, copied from the row's own rationale where it had one and written as "starting value" where it did not; tests/test_gate_thresholds_provenance.py fails on a number with neither.
`why` is the rationale the row had in scripts/gate_profiles.py before the move, kept so the reasoning is not lost.
`choices` lists the allowed values of an enumerated parameter; `unit` is present only where the unit is not obvious from the name.
Changing a `default` is a gate decision: tests/fixtures/gate/thresholds.json records it, so regenerate that deliberately and say why.

loudness.why: protected: measured faults no type of music excuses

silence.why: The numbers are the module's old constants, now readable parameters. `silence` stays protected: a declared rest exempts its window from the *measurement* (the direction sheet's `silence_after_s`), never the threshold.

shape.contrast.meaning: the piece changes level and density between its sections
shape.contrast.why: The one positive score row. Every other score row asks whether a part repeats; this one asks whether the sections differ from each other at all, which is the arc a repetition count cannot see. The spread is in MIDI velocity units: the ASAP corpus measured 5-95 percentile ranges of 36.7 (Baroque) and 53.8 (Romantic), so 12 units between two section means is below every measured piece, not a taste threshold.
